S004.note: Binding does not follow statement order, so both definitions of `pick` answer. See "Statement order" in docs/limitations.md.

S005.note: The second call also sees both definitions. Same cause as S004.

S008.note: The call after `unset -f` stays a candidate edge to the definition (reason `unset-in-view`), and definition returns the candidates. Order is not tracked. See "Statement order" in docs/limitations.md.

S031.note: A caller's `local` is offered for a read in a callee only when no declaration is in view. Here `mode=slow` is a declaration in view, so the read resolves to it.

S044.note: A call outside the subshell, command substitution or pipeline stage that confines a definition is a `candidate`/`conditional-definition` edge, and definition returns that candidate; the truth file expects none.

S057.note: A call before the `source` line still sees the sourced file: a name in file A can refer to a definition in every file reachable from a file that reaches A. See "Statement order" in docs/limitations.md.

S070.note: Declarations inside `eval` strings are not taken; only calls are read from a string. See "Functions defined by eval" in docs/limitations.md.

S074.note: Alias use is order-free, so `alias aa=...; aa` on one line resolves through the alias, although bash expands neither before the line ends. See "Aliases" in docs/limitations.md.

S075.note: `unalias NAME` is not read, so a later call still resolves through the alias. See "Aliases" in docs/limitations.md.

S101.note: After an unterminated quote the parser cuts at the failure, finds the next statement boundary at column 0 (function header, keyword, blank line) and parses the rest separately. The truth file reads the manual (the rest is quoted text). See "Unclosed quotes" in docs/limitations.md.

S150.note: The last `f` is parsed after the recovery point. Same cause as S101.
